subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Plastic Bag Charges
description: A short lesson to help you apply Plastic Bag Charges.

hook.text: Ireland introduced a 15-cent plastic bag tax. Bag use dropped 94%. A tiny charge achieved what years of environmental.

buildup.text: The charge works through loss aversion, not rational cost calculation. 15 cents is trivial.

discovery.text: The charge also changes social norms. Once most people bring reusable bags, using a plastic bag feels embarrassing.

twist.text: Free but slightly harder also works. Simply not offering bags at the counter, requiring customers to ask, reduces use.

climax.text: Plastic bag charges show that tiny financial signals combined with norm shifts can change behavior at massive scale.

punchline.text: Fifteen cents changed a nation's habit. The price was symbolic.

quiz.question: Why did a 15-cent bag charge reduce usage by 94%?
options: 15 cents was too expensive for most Irish consumers
Loss aversion made paying for a previously free item disproportionately painful
The government banned plastic bags entirely
